doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Out clean in 1953 at the Flame with blues singers
summary: After release, Ware works the Flame with Joe Joe Adams and singers like Joe Williams, Della Reese and Jimmy Witherspoon.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: When I came out, I was clean -- '53, Ike Morris Hyte has just preceeded me, he left -- that was just before he died. I was in there, he carved up some sticks and sent them down to my cell and he said to keep practicing, you know, keep your wrists up, and I did. And when I come out, I got a job at a place called the Flame -- that was on Oakwood Blav., working and a trumpet player -- a trumpet and violinist -- Melvin Porter Kilbert, Moore and alto was Killman, Earl Phillips was on drums, and Jimmy Boyle was playing piano. And we were working at a place called the Flame, and Jo Jo Joe Adams was a blues singer, and all the blues singers used to come through there -- in fact, any singer would come there -- Joe Williams, Della Reese, Betty 'Bebop' Benny Carter, and ... the fellow who wrote 'Two Years of Torture' -- oh God, a beautiful cat, Jimmy Witherspoon used to come, too. Oh, it was beautiful.
